description: This ASDSO lesson learned treats dams, hydropower stations, locks and levees as critical infrastructure that can be attacked deliberately, and pairs a general discussion with two case studies. It notes that dams are large, remote and hard to guard, that credible threats exploit site-specific weaknesses such as limited redundancy or dependence on control systems, and that a DHS resource recorded 25 physical attacks on dams between 2001 and 2011 using explosives, standoff weapons, assault teams and incendiaries. The first case is the Dnieper Hydroelectric Station, destroyed in August 1941 with about 20 tons of explosives damaging some 100 metres of dam and sending a flood wave with little warning, and struck again in 2022; the second is the 2013 intrusion into the Bowman Avenue Dam control system in New York. Coverage: three incidents in two countries plus general guidance. Access: a free web page; the licence is not stated. Caveats: casualty estimates are secondary and vary widely. It supports attack scenario, cascading failure and emergency response analysis for dams, and relates to the ASDSO timely warning lessons and the Kakhovka dam destruction case study already in the catalogue.
